label: pants-fire
speaker: Social Media / Viral Post
statement: The CDC secretly admitted in court documents that COVID vaccines contain tracking microchips.
justification: The claim cites a fabricated court document. CDC public records and independent laboratory analyses confirm no microchips or tracking devices exist in any approved vaccine.

label: false
speaker: Campaign TV Ad
statement: My opponent voted to completely eliminate Social Security benefits for all current retirees.
justification: Legislative records show the opponent voted on a broader budget amendment that proposed reducing cost-of-living adjustments by 1%, not eliminating benefits for retirees.

label: barely-true
speaker: US Senator
statement: Our state lost 50,000 manufacturing jobs during the last administration.
justification: While 50,000 jobs were lost over a decade, most of the decline occurred due to global economic trends prior to the administration in question, leaving out critical context.

label: half-true
speaker: State Governor
statement: We cut state income taxes for middle-class families by 15 percent this year.
justification: The state did reduce income tax rates for the middle tax bracket, but simultaneously increased local sales taxes, resulting in a net tax cut smaller than claimed.

label: mostly-true
speaker: Congressperson
statement: Over 80 percent of small business owners say access to affordable healthcare is a top issue.
justification: A recent National Small Business Association survey found 78% of surveyed business owners listed healthcare costs as a major operational concern, matching the claim closely.

label: true
speaker: Labor Department Official
statement: The federal minimum wage has remained at .25 per hour since July 2009.
justification: Under the Fair Labor Standards Act amendment of 2007, the federal minimum wage rose to .25 on July 24, 2009, and has not been raised by Congress since.
